text: The following table sets forth the name and position of each of our executive officers and directors, as well as their respective ages as of October 9, 2026.

Luca Santarelli, M.D. Dr. Santarelli is our Chief Executive Officer and founder and has served as the Chair of our board of directors since January 2025. He was recently the Chief Executive Officer and founder of VectivBio Holding AG, where he led VectivBio’s strategic vision, R&D and capital raising until its acquisition by Ironwood Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: IRWD), from June 2019 to June 2023. Previously, from January 2016 to June 2019, he served as Chief Executive Officer and co-founder of Therachon Holding AG that was acquired by Pfizer Inc. (NYSE: PFE). Prior to Therachon, he spent 11 years at F. Hoffmann-La Roche AG (OTC: RHHBY), most recently serving as the Senior Vice President and Head of Neuroscience, Ophthalmology and Rare Diseases, as well as Small Molecules Research where he advanced over 20 NMEs to the clinic and various NMEs to registration studies. Dr. Santarelli is also the Chair of the board of directors of Alentis Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biotech company focused on cancer and fibrosis, since June 2023 after joining its board of directors in November 2021. He previously served as a member of the board of directors of Cimeio Therapeutics, an immunotherapy company, from August 2022 until April 2025. Dr. Santarelli received his M.D. and Psychiatry Residency at the University of Turin, Italy and a postdoctoral fellowship at Columbia University, focusing on the molecular mechanisms of psychiatric disorders and adult brain stem cell biology. We believe Dr. Santarelli is qualified to serve on our board of directors because of his experience as our Chief Executive Officer and founder as well as his extensive experience with advising and leading biotechnology companies.

notes.title: Organization and business
text: Windward Bio Group AG (the “Company”) is a Swiss stock corporation whose registered office is at Aeschenplatz 6, 4052 Basel, Switzerland. The Company was incorporated on July 5, 2024, in Switzerland. It is subject to provisions of the articles of association and to article 620 et seq. of the Swiss Code of Obligations, which describes the legal requirements for corporations (“Aktiengesellschaften”).

The Company has two wholly owned subsidiaries (directly or indirectly) (the “Subsidiaries”), Windward Bio AG and Windward Bio Inc (collectively “Windward Bio” or the “Group”). The Group also controls LE2025 Therapeutics AG (“LE2025”) through contractual arrangements. The Company is the ultimate parent of Windward Bio. Windward Bio is a clinical-stage biotechnology company with deep discovery, development, and commercialization expertise, committed to transforming the treatment of people living with advanced immunological conditions. Its lead program is WIN378, a potentially novel, long-acting, anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody. The pipeline also includes WIN027, a clinical-stage, long-acting anti-TSLPxIL-13 bi-specific, which has broad therapeutic application across immunological diseases.

notes.title: Basis of preparation
text: These consolidated financial statements are the first consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards, as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (“IFRS”). The consolidated financial statements have been prepared on a historical cost basis and are presented in United States dollars (“USD” or “$”). All amounts disclosed in the financial statements and notes have been rounded to the nearest thousand unless otherwise stated. The consolidated financial statements were approved and authorized for issue by our board of directors on July 24, 2026.
First time adoption of IFRS

IFRS 1 allows first-time adopters certain exemptions from the retrospective application of certain requirements under IFRS. None of the exemptions have been applied because they were not significant at the date of first-time application.

costs.heading: Operating expenses
costs.text:
Our operating expenses consist of (i) research and development expenses and (ii) general and administrative expenses.

Our research and development expenses primarily consist of internal and external expenses incurred to support research and development activities including our clinical trials and development of future product candidates. These expenses include:

• Services and materials expenses, including expenses incurred under arrangements with third-party CROs, CDMOs, third-party consultants and other advisors

• Intellectual property and related future payments dependent on the achievement of development and regulatory milestones

• Personnel-related costs, including salaries, bonuses, benefits and share-based compensation for employees engaged in research and development activities

• Depreciation expenses related to assets used in research and development activities

We do not capitalize any of these development costs that we incur, as the costs do not meet the criteria for capitalization in IFRS. Instead, we expense research and development costs as incurred.

rd.heading: Other Research and Development Obligations
rd.text: In the normal course of our business, we enter into arrangements with CROs, CDMOs and other third-party vendors for nonclinical studies, clinical trials, testing and manufacturing services. These contracts are generally cancellable by us upon prior notice. Payments due upon cancellation generally consist only of payments for services provided or expenses incurred, including non-cancellable obligations of the service providers, up to the date of cancellation.
